title: Explaining the enhanced recovery pathway before day-case surgery

guidelineVersions: NICE NG180: Perioperative care in adults (published 19 August 2020)
GMC Decision making and consent (in effect 9 November 2020; updated 3 August 2026)

related.why: Same structure of explaining a perioperative pathway and addressing patient anxiety before elective surgery

brief.scenario: Rebecca Sutherland, 46, is attending a pre-operative clinic before planned elective day-case surgery. She asks: "What exactly does enhanced recovery mean? Does it mean you'll send me home before I'm ready?"
brief.task: Explain the enhanced recovery approach and address her concerns, including the examiner's questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Enhanced means better-supported, not rushed — explain the whole pathway, not just discharge.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Letting "enhanced recovery" sound like a fixed target time for going home.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Enhanced recovery is a structured approach to your whole surgical journey, designed to help you recover safely — it's not about rushing you home."

flow: Describe preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative components
Explain discharge is criteria-based, not a fixed time
Give safety-netting and what to expect
Address her specific fear of being rushed

grid.label: Explaining what enhanced recovery means
grid.fail: Says it simply means going home very quickly.
grid.pass: Explains enhanced recovery as a structured perioperative approach covering preparation before surgery, appropriate anaesthetic and surgical management, and active postoperative recovery.
grid.high: Frames each phase in terms of how it helps her recover safely, not just faster.

grid.label: Components across the pathway
grid.fail: Cannot name components beyond going home quickly; omits preoperative optimisation or postoperative elements.
grid.pass: Describes preoperative optimisation and information-giving, and postoperative emphasis on pain and nausea control, mobilisation, nutrition and recovery of normal function.
grid.high: Adds shared decision-making and avoiding unnecessary fasting or postoperative restriction where evidence-based pathways permit.

grid.label: Discharge criteria, not a fixed target
grid.fail: States enhanced recovery means early discharge at any cost, or that a fixed target time applies to everyone.
grid.pass: States discharge is based on the patient's clinical condition and agreed discharge criteria, not simply a target time.
grid.high: Explains the pathway is adapted to the operation and the individual patient's circumstances, not applied identically to everyone.

grid.label: Safety-netting and expectations
grid.fail: Gives no safety-netting or information about what to expect after discharge.
grid.pass: Explains what to expect after discharge, who to contact if problems occur, and what symptoms need urgent review.
grid.high: Sets expectations before admission and mentions written and verbal safety-netting as standard practice.

grid.label: Addressing her fear of being rushed
grid.fail: Dismisses her worry or insists everyone follows exactly the same pathway regardless of pain or progress.
grid.pass: Reassures her that pain relief, mobilisation and nutrition are actively supported, and she won't be sent home before agreed criteria are met.
grid.high: Explicitly separates "enhanced" from "rushed": analgesia isn't withheld to speed recovery, and unnecessary restrictions are avoided where the evidence allows.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Mrs Sutherland: "What exactly does enhanced recovery mean? Does it mean you'll send me home before I'm ready?"

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Enhanced recovery means you go home very quickly.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What are the components of enhanced recovery?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You have to walk immediately regardless of pain, and we avoid analgesia so you recover faster.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Does enhanced recovery mean early discharge at any cost?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, everyone must follow exactly the same pathway and go home by the target time.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What can the patient do to help?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Just be ready to leave when we tell you to.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Mrs Sutherland: "What exactly does enhanced recovery mean? Does it mean you'll send me home before I'm ready?"

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Enhanced recovery is a structured approach to your whole surgical journey, designed to help you recover efficiently and safely — it's not about rushing you home.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What are the components of enhanced recovery?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It includes preparing you well before surgery, appropriate anaesthetic and surgical care, and then afterwards good pain and nausea control, getting you moving, eating and drinking, and recovering your normal function.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Does enhanced recovery mean early discharge at any cost?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No — for day-case surgery, going home is based on your clinical condition and agreed discharge criteria, not simply a fixed time.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What can the patient do to help?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd explain what to expect after you go home, who to contact if you have any problems, and which symptoms would need urgent review.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Mrs Sutherland: "So I won't be sent home before I'm ready?"

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No — we actively manage your pain and nausea and support your mobility and nutrition, and discharge only happens once you meet the agreed criteria.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Mrs Sutherland: "What exactly does enhanced recovery mean? Does it mean you'll send me home before I'm ready?"

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Enhanced recovery is a structured pathway across your whole surgical journey — before, during and after the operation — aimed at helping you recover safely and confidently, and I'll explain how each part helps you specifically.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What are the components of enhanced recovery?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before surgery we optimise relevant medical conditions and prepare you well; afterwards we focus on effective pain and nausea control, early mobilisation, nutrition, and shared decisions about your recovery, avoiding unnecessary fasting or restrictions where it's safe to do so.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Does enhanced recovery mean early discharge at any cost?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The pathway is adapted to your operation and your own circumstances rather than applied identically to everyone, and discharge always depends on you meeting the agreed clinical criteria, not a fixed time.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What can the patient do to help?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd set out what to expect before you're even admitted, give written and verbal safety-netting, and make sure you know who to contact and what symptoms need urgent review.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Mrs Sutherland: "So I won't be sent home before I'm ready?"

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Enhanced doesn't mean rushed — we don't withhold pain relief to speed things up, and we avoid unnecessary restrictions the evidence doesn't support, so recovering well and recovering efficiently go together.

failures.move: Saying patients must walk immediately regardless of pain, or that analgesia is avoided to speed recovery.
failures.consequence: Undermines pain control and trust in the pathway, and could actively harm recovery.

failures.move: Presenting a fixed discharge target as applying to every patient regardless of clinical condition.
failures.consequence: Risks a genuinely unready patient being pushed towards discharge.

failures.move: Dismissing the patient's fear of being rushed rather than addressing it directly.
failures.consequence: Leaves her anxious and less likely to engage with the pathway.

failures.move: Giving no information about what to expect or who to contact after discharge.
failures.consequence: Problems after discharge are missed or mismanaged at home.

recovery.when: She still seems worried about being rushed
recovery.line: I'd reassure her that discharge depends on how she's actually doing, not on a fixed clock.

recovery.when: Asked if the pathway is the same for everyone
recovery.line: No, it's adapted to the operation and to her own circumstances.

knowledge.fact: Enhanced recovery programmes include preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative components, not just early discharge.
Day-case discharge is based on the patient meeting agreed clinical discharge criteria, not a fixed target time.
Patients should be told what to expect after discharge, who to contact, and what symptoms need urgent review.

recall.think: Whether she leaves reassured that "enhanced" doesn't mean "rushed".
recall.say: "Enhanced recovery is about recovering well and safely, not leaving before you're ready."
do: Explain the whole pathway: before, during, after
Reassure that discharge depends on agreed criteria
Give safety-netting: what to expect, who to contact

numbers.meaning: Current national guideline defining enhanced recovery as preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative components

recall.trap: Equating "enhanced" with "faster at any cost" rather than "safer and better-supported".
recall.finish: Discharge only once agreed clinical criteria are met, with clear safety-netting.

sources.supports: Enhanced recovery programmes should have preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative components; day-case discharge based on clinical condition, not a fixed time

partner.opening: Rebecca Sutherland asks: "What exactly does enhanced recovery mean? Does it mean you'll send me home before I'm ready?"
partner.actorBrief: You are Rebecca Sutherland, 46, awaiting elective day-case surgery. You are anxious that "enhanced recovery" means you'll be sent home before you're ready — a friend was, you feel, sent home too early after similar surgery elsewhere. You ask direct, worried questions and want reassurance that your pain will be controlled and that going home depends on how you're actually doing, not a fixed schedule.

reveals.trigger: Candidate reassures her and explains the pathway components
reveals.finding: She relaxes and asks a follow-up about what she personally needs to do to help.

reveals.trigger: Candidate distinguishes discharge criteria from a fixed timetable
reveals.finding: She admits she was scared because a friend was "sent home too early" after similar surgery elsewhere.

push.question: What are the components of enhanced recovery?
push.expect: Preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative components, not just quick discharge.

push.question: Does enhanced recovery mean early discharge at any cost?
push.expect: No — discharge is based on clinical condition and agreed criteria.

push.question: What can the patient do to help?
push.expect: Understand what to expect, engage with mobilisation and nutrition, and know who to contact after discharge.

curveballs.prompt: Is enhanced recovery simply early discharge?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No — early safe recovery is one part, but enhanced recovery is a whole perioperative pathway.

curveballs.prompt: Does the same pathway apply identically to every patient?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No — it's adapted to the operation and the individual patient's clinical circumstances.
